leaf.text:
LWP is obsolete. It is not supported in Zen and is now removed from AMD Fam15/16 CPUs through security-mitigations microcode updates. On the Xen development mailing list, AMD engineers confirmed that it will not be supported in the future: https://lore.kernel.org/all/20190520184306.GC23047@amd.com
Fill the LWP entries for completeness, and for legacy CPUs, as it is still documented in the AMD programmer's manual.

bit0.desc: LWP is available to application programs (supported by OS)

bit1.desc: LWPVAL instruction (EventId=1) is supported by OS

bit2.desc: Instructions Retired Event (EventId=2) is supported by OS

bit3.desc: Branch Retired Event (EventId=3) is supported by OS

bit4.desc: DCache Miss Event (EventId=4) is supported by OS

bit5.desc: CPU Clocks Not Halted event (EventId=5) is supported by OS

bit6.desc: CPU Reference clocks Not Halted event (EventId=6) is supported by OS

bit29.desc: LWP sampling in continuous mode is supported by OS

bit30.desc: Performance Time Stamp Counter in event records is supported by OS

bit31.desc: Interrupt on threshold overflow is supported by OS

bit0.desc: LWP Control Block size, in quadwords

bit8.desc: LWP event record size, in bytes

bit16.desc: LWP max supported EventId value (EventID 255 not included)

bit24.desc: LWP events area offset in the LWP Control Block

bit0.desc: Num of bits in cache latency counters (10 to 31)

bit5.desc: Cache miss events report the data address of the reference

bit6.desc: Amount by which cache latency is rounded

bit16.desc: LWP event ring buffer min size, in units of 32 event records

bit28.desc: Branches Retired events can be filtered

bit29.desc: IP filtering (IPI, IPF, BaseIP, and LimitIP @ LWPCP) supported

bit30.desc: Cache-related events can be filtered by cache level

bit31.desc: Cache-related events can be filtered by latency

bit1.desc: LWPVAL instruction (EventId=1) is available in HW

bit2.desc: Instructions Retired Event (EventId=2) is available in HW

bit3.desc: Branch Retired Event (EventId=3) is available in HW

bit4.desc: DCache Miss Event (EventId=4) is available in HW

bit5.desc: CPU Clocks Not Halted event (EventId=5) is available in HW

bit6.desc: CPU Reference clocks Not Halted event (EventId=6) is available in HW

bit29.desc: LWP sampling in continuous mode is available in HW

bit30.desc: Performance Time Stamp Counter in event records is available in HW

bit31.desc: Interrupt on threshold overflow is available in HW
